titulo: First Steps in German: Your First Real-World Interaction

aula.objetivo: By the end of this lesson, understand a short exchange, distinguish key German sounds from English, decode common spelling patterns and greet someone confidently.

blocos.titulo: Hallo! Wie geht’s? / Hi! How are you?
blocos.contexto: Anna and Ben meet on the street. Listen without the translation first. Who asks the first question, and how does the conversation end?

blocos.explicacao: Use «Hallo» when you greet someone informally and «Tschüs» when you say goodbye. «Guten Morgen» is a morning greeting, «Guten Tag» is a daytime greeting and «Guten Abend» is used in the evening. «Gute Nacht» is normally said when someone is going to bed, not when you arrive. To ask a friend how they are, say «Wie geht’s?». A natural answer is «Gut, danke! Und dir?» — Fine, thanks! And you? With strangers, use a more formal greeting and consider «Wie geht es Ihnen?» instead of informal «Wie geht’s?».
blocos.comparacao: English works the same way here: «good evening» when you arrive and «good night» when you go to bed. German also has two expressions: «Guten Abend» on arriving and «Gute Nacht» before sleeping.

erros.errado: Gute Nacht, when arriving at a party in the evening
erros.motivo: «Gute Nacht» is only said when parting, to someone going to sleep. When you arrive, say «Guten Abend».

erros.errado: Guten Tag, at eight in the evening
erros.motivo: In the evening the greeting changes to «Guten Abend». «Guten Tag» is for the daytime.

blocos.titulo: Anna im Café / Anna in the café
blocos.ru: Guten Morgen! Anna ist im Café. Ben ist auch da. Anna sagt: Hallo, Ben! Wie geht’s? Ben sagt: Gut, danke! Und dir? Anna sagt: Auch gut, danke. Anna trinkt Tee. Ben trinkt Wasser. Das Café ist gut. Dann sagt Ben: Tschüs, Anna! Anna sagt: Tschüs, Ben!
blocos.pt: Good morning! Anna is at the café. Ben is there too. Anna says: Hi, Ben! How are you? Ben says: Fine, thanks! And you? Anna says: Also fine, thanks. Anna drinks tea. Ben drinks water. The café is good. Then Ben says: Bye, Anna! Anna says: Bye, Ben!

perguntas.pergunta: What does Anna drink and what does Ben drink?
perguntas.resposta: Anna drinks tea («Tee») and Ben drinks water («Wasser»).

perguntas.pergunta: What question does Anna ask to find out whether Ben is well?

itens.explicacao: «Guten Tag» is the daytime greeting. In «Guten Abend» you would hear «AH-bent» at the end, and in «Gute Nacht» you would hear the harsh «ch» of «nahkht».
The question starts with «vee», the German «w» sounding like «v», and ends in «GAYTS». «Und dir?» starts with «oont» and «Guten Morgen» is a greeting, not a question.
Write «Danke». The final «e» is sounded, «DAHN-kuh», and the word is the same for a man or a woman.

itens.enunciado: Which greeting is used in the morning?
itens.explicacao: «Morgen» means morning. «Abend» is evening, and «Nacht» is the time to sleep.

itens.enunciado: Listen, repeat out loud and then show the answer.

itens.explicacao: «Tschüs» is the informal goodbye, which reads «chüs». Thank you is «Danke», and please is «Bitte».
After saying you are well, you thank the person for asking with «danke». «Tschüs» is goodbye and «bitte» would be «please».
When you arrive in the evening you say «Guten Abend». «Guten Morgen» is for the morning, and «Nacht» is kept for «Gute Nacht», when going to sleep.
To greet a friend you say «Hallo». «Tschüs» is for saying goodbye and «Danke» is thank you.

itens.enunciado: Listen, repeat out loud and then show the answer.

itens.explicacao: The question starts with the question word «Wie», how, and then comes «geht’s».

itens.enunciado: Put in order: «Fine, thanks! And you?»
itens.explicacao: First the answer «Gut, danke!» and then the question handed back, «Und dir?».
The greeting «Guten Morgen» comes first, in full, and the person's name comes last.

itens.enunciado: Listen, repeat out loud and then show the answer.

itens.explicacao: «Auch gut» means also fine, and the thanks «danke» closes the sentence.

itens.enunciado: Write one greeting and one goodbye in German. Example: use Hallo and Tschüs.
Write a natural two-line exchange asking a friend how they are. Include their reply.
itens.respostaEsperada: Wie geht’s? Gut, danke! Und dir?

itens.enunciado: Write the greeting for arriving in the evening, then the expression used when someone goes to sleep.

blocos.enunciado: Final mission: play Anna and Ben without reading the English translations. Open with «Hallo!», ask «Wie geht’s?», reply «Gut, danke! Und dir?» and close with «Tschüs!». Then choose «Guten Morgen», «Guten Tag» or «Guten Abend» for the situation. Explain why «Gute Nacht» is not the normal greeting when arriving at an evening event.
Listen to «Eis», «Bier», «Schule», «Sport», «Haus», «ich» and «Buch» and say which letter combination appears in each one.
